accepted.description: RETAINED, REDUNDANT: every registry row now carries the same acceptance facts, and more, in its account block. Kept so answers stay shape-compatible with consumers written against earlier versions.

QuestAccountState.description: Where one account stands on one quest, served as the facts that discriminate it rather than as a single label. The four combinations are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so any consumer vocabulary maps on without loss: !accepted = never accepted; accepted && complete = already finished; accepted && !complete && objectivesMet = unfinished with the work done; accepted && !complete && !objectivesMet = unfinished with work outstanding. requirementsMet answers whether a quest not yet accepted can be accepted at all.

objectivesMet.description: This layer's evaluation of the objectives it can read — NOT a promise that the finishing transaction will succeed. A consumer needing that guarantee must have the chain simulate the act. The field is not named 'completable' for exactly this reason.

objectives.description: Present only for accepted quests. Accrual objectives count from a snapshot taken at acceptance; before acceptance no snapshot exists and the comparison would run against zero, reading an account's lifetime total as if it were progress. Serving that would hand out a number the world does not hold, so unaccepted rows carry thresholds without progress.

current.description: Progress on the basis named below. Absent where there is nothing to count (boolean objectives) and for a finished quest, whose objectives stop being evaluated. No number is synthesized in either case.

basis.description: since-acceptance = accrual counted from the moment of acceptance, not a balance: spending what you accrued does not un-count it, and a balance held before acceptance does not count toward it. current = the present value (a balance, a level, a score). boolean = met or not, with nothing to count. unknown = a handler this version does not evaluate.
